name: Australia
alt: A world map with one entire island-sized landmass highlighted, surrounded completely by ocean, off by itself.
facts: It's the only country on Earth that is also an entire continent all by itself.
Almost all of its people live clustered near the coast, leaving its vast red center mostly empty.
It's home to more kinds of venomous snakes than any other country in the world.

name: Fiji
alt: A world map zoomed into a cluster of small islands scattered alone in the middle of a wide blue ocean, far from any other highlighted land.
facts: It's made up of more than 300 islands, but only about a third of them have anyone living on them.
A single friendly word — 'Bula' — gets shouted as a greeting pretty much everywhere you go here.
Its national rugby team is so beloved that the whole country basically pauses for big matches.

name: New Zealand
alt: A world map with two long, narrow highlighted islands stacked one above the other, set apart in the ocean southeast of a much larger landmass.
facts: There are still several times more sheep here than people, even after decades of the gap shrinking.
It was one of the last large landmasses on Earth to be settled by people, only a few hundred years before Europeans showed up.
Its dramatic mountains and green hills got turned into an entire fantasy world for the big screen.

name: Papua New Guinea
alt: A world map with a highlighted landmass on the eastern half of a large tropical island, just north of a much bigger highlighted island-continent.
facts: More than 800 different languages are spoken here — more than in any other country on Earth.
So much of its land is steep mountains and thick rainforest that some remote villages can only be reached by small plane.
It's home to the world's largest butterfly, with wings about as wide as a dinner plate.

name: Solomon Islands
alt: A world map with a scattered chain of small highlighted islands stretching in a loose line across the ocean, northeast of a much larger landmass.
facts: It's made up of almost 1,000 islands, though nearly everyone lives on just a handful of the larger ones.
Its coral reefs are so packed with fish and sea life that scientists rank them among the richest underwater worlds on Earth.
After a huge World War II naval battle, its waters earned the nickname 'Ironbottom Sound' for all the sunken ships resting there.

name: Vanuatu
alt: A world map with a thin, scattered chain of small highlighted islands shaped like a 'Y', alone in the ocean.
facts: Some of its islands have active volcanoes you can actually hike right up to the rim of and peer inside.
On one island, villagers tie vines to their ankles and leap from tall wooden towers — a tradition some say inspired modern bungee jumping.
It's regularly ranked among the happiest places on Earth, despite facing more natural disasters than almost anywhere else.
